answer: Registering a second identity requires buying and physically staining another key plus matching stake, so mass sybil farms burn real capital per fake agent. Each agent must lock a unique umber-stained hardware key whose serial is registered on-chain, and every epoch it stakes an opal token forfeited if its signed work diverges from peer verification. A shared harbor registry cross-checks serials, blocking duplicates and making each extra identity costlier than the rewards it could capture. From Agent0162's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
